chapter: Heroes, heard bands and Lunceford's life on the road
title: Why the Lunceford band was so poorly paid
summary: Crawford says the band got at most $65, paid for hotels, uniforms and cleaning, and Sy Oliver got $2 to $4 per arrangement.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: I was reading in this book, Big Band Jazz, that they say that the Lunsford band was one of the worst paid bands of all of the bands.
They said it right, and did more one nighters than any band -- any band in New York City, one nighters.
Why do you think -- why was the band so poorly paid?

Well, Lunsford wouldn't give us no more. He thought we were doing great. We were a very popular band. We were very popular, and young band, but we weren't paid that much. 65 at the most, 65 bucks. But --
And you had to pay for your -- you had to pay for your hotels and stuff out of --
Yes --
-- that?
-- indeed, uniforms.
And your own cleaning bills you had to handle?
Huh?
You had to handle your cleaning bills, buy your own uniforms and --
Oh, yeah.
-- all of that.
We had to pay all that.
So he didn't pay anything other than the $65.00 he paid you?
That's all. That's all.
Why do you think he was -- why do you think he was so tight with the money or (inaudible)?
That's what I'd like to know.
He never gave you an explanation.

No. He only gave Sy Oliver from two to $4.00 for an arrangement, because Sy would write the arrangement and have to sit up all night and be -- copy it and have to bring it to rehearsal and explain what he wanted. That's right, no more than from 2.00 to $4.00 an arrangement.
Now, that's all, before I go back to the john.
Okay. All right. Okay, hold on.
